description:
From the 2026-08-19 gap audit of #152 vs ../foundationdb. FDB seeds every new commit proxy with the FULL system-key state before it serves anything (CommitProxyServer.actor.cpp:77 broadcastTxnRequest(TxnStateRequest); requests refused until txnStateStore is valid). Bedrock has no counterpart: a recovered proxy starts at Metadata.new() and converges only to what THIS epoch commits. The recovery system transaction rewrites config/layout families, but materializer_keys/ has no writer at all, and the shard families are skipped when shard_layout is nil/empty (persistence_phase.ex:330). The coverage-gap fail-fast's premise ("recovery rebuilds proxies with full state", commit_proxy/server.ex) is only true for rewritten families.

Non-consequential today (nothing reads proxy Metadata but the window applier), but BOTH q67.9 read-path options ("clients read map from metadata shard or proxy MetadataAccumulator") and q67.21's materializer_keys writer presuppose post-recovery completeness.

Decide and implement ONE of: (a) PersistencePhase clear+rewrites every proxy-visible family each recovery, including materializer_keys/ once q67.21 writes it (resolves q67.21's open ownership question as recovery-written); or (b) seed proxy Metadata from a durable metadata-shard read at recover_from (closer to FDB's TxnStateRequest). Decision gates q67.9's read path.
title: Proxy metadata bootstrap: decide full-rewrite vs seeded recover_from (FDB TxnStateRequest analogue)
